title: Pod stuck terminating due to zombie container lingering
body:
### Description

On a couple separate GKE clusters we've seen an issue that during a rolling restart of a deployment or stateful set, one of the pods remains stuck in `Terminating` due to a "zombie" container lingering in containerd, meaning that `containerd` believes the container still exists and is still running yet there is no process for it. I haven't found a way to convince containerd to delete this container/task, it just lingers indefinitely.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

We don't have reliable steps to reproduce the issue, our CD system occasionally runs into this, maybe once a week across thousands of pods.

### Describe the results you received and expected

`containerd` should not let this dead container linger as there is no process for it anymore, so that `kubelet` can reap the pod and let it terminate.

### What version of containerd are you using?

containerd github.com/containerd/containerd 1.7.19 4e1fe7492b9df85914c389d1f15a3ceedbb280ac

```
  Container Runtime Version:  containerd://1.7.19

```

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
The io_uring issue is documented for GKE [here](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/troubleshooting/known-issues#pods-using-io-uring-related-syscalls-stuck-in-terminating).

I'm going to lock this issue.  There are too many different bugs being discussed here.  The original bug (stuck exit processing in containerd) was fixed by https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/10651, the io_uring issue is a kernel bug, and RCU soft lockup looks like a different kernel bug.

Please open new issues if you run into pods stuck terminating and they are _not_ fixed by either https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/10651 or updating the kernel.
